answers.stem_only: Move the VPN connections from the virtual private gateway to a transit gateway with ECMP support turned on, and switch the connections to dynamic (BGP) routing so the same prefixes are advertised on all tunnels; ECMP then spreads traffic across tunnels and scales by adding connections.
Maximum resiliency model: two Direct Connect locations, each with two connections terminating on separate devices, so a device, connection or whole location can fail.
Create a Direct Connect gateway, put a private virtual interface on it, and associate the virtual private gateways of both VPCs (any Region) with the Direct Connect gateway.
AWS Client VPN endpoint associated with the VPC subnets, using SAML 2.0 federated authentication with the existing IdP; users connect with the AWS provided client.

Replace the VPN backup with a second Direct Connect connection of the same capacity at a different Direct Connect location, so the backup carries the full load and no single location is a point of failure.
Configure the second tunnel of the existing VPN connection on the customer gateway device; AWS updates one tunnel at a time, so traffic fails over to the other tunnel.
AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the internet from the existing IPsec router (customer gateway) to a virtual private gateway on the VPC; quick to set up, encrypted, fine for low traffic.

MACsec is only for dedicated connections at higher speeds, not a 1 Gbps hosted connection, and Direct Connect is not encrypted by default; run an IPsec Site-to-Site VPN over the Direct Connect connection.
A 200 Mbps hosted connection ordered through a Direct Connect Partner, with a private virtual interface to the VPC; no equipment at the Direct Connect location and no oversized dedicated port.

On the existing endpoint: add a route for 172.16.0.0/16 through the associated subnet plus an authorization rule for it, and turn on split-tunnel (modifiable in place) so only routed VPC and on-premises traffic uses the tunnel.
Order an AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection for consistent performance and run an AWS Site-to-Site VPN (IPsec) over it from the data center router for encryption.
Turn on MACsec on the 10 Gbps dedicated connection and configure the matching keys (CKN/CAK) on the router; layer-2 encryption without the IPsec MTU and throughput penalty.
